text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani says at budget briefing that Nigeria won't be rushed into privatisation of its state enterprises.
- Federal government allocates $230 million to state-run oil company NNPC for rehabilitation of Nigeria's four refineries and products distribution pipelines.
- Test production begins at the 30 million naira castor oil plant located in northern Kaduna.
- Decision of state-run Nigerian Ports Authority to withdraw credit facility granted NNPC for ports charges on its vessels may trigger fuel shortages.
- Nigeria reassessing joint venture deals with six oil multinationals following losses, Finance Minister Ani says.
- Nigeria plans to invoke its extradition agreement with other countries in effort to prosecute people who failed to execute government contracts.

- Lagos state police commissioner Abubakar Tsav has been briefed on a cache of arms and ammunition discovered in a lorry at the weekend by "Operation Sweep" -- a combined police, military and naval security force.
- Aviation ministry panel report rules out sabotage in the crash of a Nigerian airliner last November in which all 142 people on board died, according to newspapers investigation.
- Local investors take over remaining 9.9 percent paidup share capital of U.K-based Standard Chartered Bank which divested from Nigeria's First Bank last year.
- Federal government to liquidate distressed commercial and merchant banks that are not re-capitalised by end-March, Ani says.
